prerequisites: Basic knowledge of chemistry, physics and mathematics acquired at secondary school
University course in Mathematical Analysis I (with exercises)

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the knowledge of the fundamentals of chemistry and the strategies for using chemical models to solve simple problems.
Stimulate students' ability to abstract and apply theoretical models through experimental practice in the chemistry laboratory strongly integrated with theoretical aspects.
Understand the main methods of modern chemistry and acquire the ability to understand the patterns of inorganic systems of interest in electronics.
Apply the acquired knowledge to the characterisation of matter (mainly semiconductors) from various chemical and physico-chemical aspects.
Understand, critically discuss and present the results obtained and the approximations made through written reports of laboratory experiments.
Develop the ability to present the data obtained in an effective and concise way, to express the concepts learnt in an appropriate language and to lead a discussion on the topics covered.
Acquire the methodological tools to continue their studies and to organise their own updating.
Interpret and generalise experimental data from laboratory experiments into abstract patterns.

syllabus_topics: Atoms, molecules, ions and chemical structures
Chemical bonds in and between molecules: liquids, solids and gases and their transformation and reactivity
Fundamentals of organic chemistry: classification of functional groups
Properties of metals, insulators and semiconductors
Thermodynamics and reference to phase transition diagrams
The nature of chemical reactions: moles, molecular weights and grams as units for quantitative description of chemical transformations, with special emphasis on combustion reactions
Chemical equilibrium and spontaneous chemical reactions in the gas phase and aqueous media
Electrochemistry and chemical reactions involving electrical work
Exercises on the main topics covered, self-assessment exercises and collaborative correction

assessment_methods.method: Written test (numerical exercises and theoretical questions)

assessment_rules: The final assessment consists of two parts: one relating to theory and exercises and the other relating to laboratory activities. The laboratory activity is assessed by means of a report which the student can only produce if he/she carries out the activity at times other than the official timetable. In the absence of this report, the grade will be determined by the theory and practical part only and cannot exceed 28/30. An oral examination may also be conducted in person to supplement the grade obtained in the written test.
